title: Labor Studies
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units

program.section_heading: Labor Studies - Certificate of Achievement: City
outcomes: Identify the role of working people in the U.S. and analyze how concepts of work informed the origins of unionization in the country as well as theoretical developments of labor as a field of study.
Describe current and emerging labor issues in ways that demonstrate awareness of issues of equity such as race, ethnicity and gender in the labor force, immigrant workers, and young workers.
Identify strategies used in a variety of work settings and organizations and analyze for their effectiveness in promoting fair and equitable labor practices.

notes: The learning outcomes are introduced as outcomes for students who complete 'the Labor Studies Program'; they are printed on this certificate's page and recorded as this award's outcomes.

Careers were read from the summary, which names 'union members, organizers, and officers' and 'non-profit community organizing work'. 'union members' was not recorded as a career because it is a membership role rather than an occupation; a reviewer may wish to check this.
The 'Semester Units: 12.0' heading and 'Total Units: 12.0' both state the 12-unit total.
